summary: Backend registry and path-to-provider detection. register_storage_backend(provider_type) is a class decorator that maps a CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE to a backend class; get_storage_backend instantiates the registered class with the profile, connection and optional auth_strategy/location_check, and raises BackendNotImplementedError for known-but-unimplemented providers. detect_provider_from_path maps a path's scheme (via location.identify_scheme and the SCHEMES table) to a provider type. Built-in backends (local, S3 family, SFTP, HTTP) load lazily on first lookup, and caller registrations override them.
key_functions: register_storage_backend(provider_type) -> Callable[[type], type] — decorator; loads built-ins first so caller registration wins

get_storage_backend(provider_type, storage_profile, *, connection=None, auth_strategy=None, location_check=None) — instantiate backend; BackendNotImplementedError for enum members without a backend, ValueError for unknown values
get_registered_backends() -> dict[CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE, type] — copy of the registry (README support matrix must match)
detect_provider_from_path(path) -> CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE — scheme dispatch; '' (bare/empty path) maps to local; ValueError for unknown schemes or schemes with no provider
ensure_backends_loaded() — imports storage.backends so decorators run
extension_points: Register a custom backend class for any CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE with @register_storage_backend; it overrides the built-in
Backend constructors receive (storage_profile, connection=..., [auth_strategy=...], [location_check=...]); accepting auth_strategy (explicitly or via **kwargs) is required for managed OAuth2
Implement the storage.protocols capability protocols a la carte; the facade checks them with isinstance
lifecycle_notes: Base-install safe: backends package imports no SDK at import time (enforced by tests/test_slim_install.py)
Backends are stateless handlers; connection lifecycle belongs to connections/ and the facade
auth_strategy forwarding is guarded: a backend whose ctor cannot accept it raises BackendNotImplementedError rather than TypeError (only HTTP accepts it today)
documentation_hooks: Backend support matrix generated from get_registered_backends()
Extending: writing and registering a custom storage backend
Path dispatch: scheme -> provider mapping and error cases
Architecture: profile registry vs backend registry and the implemented-flag drift test
examples: examples/path_dispatch/example.py — detect_provider_from_path over bare, s3, r2, https etc. paths
risks: clear_registry() empties the dict, but ensure_backends_loaded() will not re-register built-ins because the backends package is already in sys.modules; after clear_registry the built-ins are gone for the rest of the process (tests snapshot and restore _backend_registry manually instead)
The registry is process-global mutable state: a third-party registration silently replaces a built-in backend for every facade in the process
detect_provider_from_path and get_storage_backend raise ValueError for unknown schemes/types rather than a StorageError subclass

evidence.detail: get_storage_backend and detect_provider_from_path are root exports
register_storage_backend calls ensure_backends_loaded() before registering (caller wins)
Fixture snapshots/restores reg._backend_registry rather than relying on clear_registry
Five commits 2026-10-28/29 (lazy loading, caller-wins, location_check, base install): evolving
